title: 101. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Converting Rates Between Time Units
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Converting Speed from Kilometres per Hour to Metres per Second
questions.learningObjective: Convert a speed given in \(\text{km/h}\) to \(\text{m/s}\) using standard time and distance conversions.
questions.question: Convert \(36\text{ km/h}\) to metres per second.
questions.explanation: Use \(1\text{ km}=1{,}000\text{ m}\) and \(1\text{ h}=3{,}600\text{ s}\). The numerical conversion is \(36\times\frac{1{,}000}{3{,}600}=36\times\frac{5}{18}=10\), so the speed is \(10\text{ m/s}\). The alternative multiplies by \(3.6\), reversing the speed conversion.
questions.hint: Track the distance unit and the time unit separately.

questions.concept: Converting Speed from Metres per Second to Kilometres per Hour
questions.learningObjective: Convert a speed given in \(\text{m/s}\) to \(\text{km/h}\).
questions.question: Convert \(15\text{ m/s}\) to kilometres per hour.
questions.explanation:
Use \(1\text{ m/s}=3.6\text{ km/h}\). Thus
\(15\times 3.6=54\text{ km/h}\). The alternative divides by \(3.6\) rather than multiplying.
questions.hint: Track the distance unit and the time unit separately.

questions.concept: Converting Speed from Kilometres per Hour to Metres per Second
questions.learningObjective: Convert a larger speed from \(\text{km/h}\) to \(\text{m/s}\).
questions.question: Convert \(90\text{ km/h}\) to metres per second.
questions.explanation:
Using the factor \(\frac{5}{18}\),
\(90\times \frac{5}{18}=25\text{ m/s}\). The alternative \(324\) multiplies by \(3.6\), reversing the speed conversion.
questions.hint: Write a unit conversion that cancels both the kilometres and the hours.

questions.concept: Converting Speed from Metres per Second to Kilometres per Hour
questions.learningObjective: Convert a speed in \(\text{m/s}\) to \(\text{km/h}\) in a practical context.
questions.question: A train travels at \(20\text{ m/s}\). What is this speed in kilometres per hour?
questions.explanation:
Since \(1\text{ m/s}=3.6\text{ km/h}\),
\(20\times 3.6=72\text{ km/h}\). The alternative divides by \(3.6\) rather than multiplying.
questions.hint: Track the distance unit and the time unit separately.

questions.concept: Converting a Rate from per Minute to per Hour
questions.learningObjective: Convert a rate given per minute to the equivalent rate per hour.
questions.question: A pump moves water at \(5\text{ L/min}\). What is this rate in litres per hour?
questions.explanation:
There are \(60\text{ min}\) in one hour, so
\(5\times 60=300\text{ L/h}\). The alternative divides by the number of minutes in an hour rather than multiplying.
questions.hint: Decide how changing the time unit changes a rate.

questions.concept: Converting a Rate from per Hour to per Minute
questions.learningObjective: Convert a rate given per hour to the equivalent rate per minute.
questions.question: A machine produces \(240\text{ L/h}\). What is this rate in litres per minute?
questions.explanation:
There are \(60\text{ min}\) in one hour, so
\(240\div 60=4\text{ L/min}\). The alternative multiplies by the number of minutes in an hour instead of dividing.
questions.hint: Write a unit conversion that cancels the unwanted time unit.

questions.concept: Converting a Rate from per Second to per Minute
questions.learningObjective: Convert a rate given per second to the equivalent rate per minute.
questions.question: A reaction produces \(3\text{ g/s}\). What is this rate in grams per minute?
questions.explanation:
There are \(60\text{ s}\) in one minute, so
\(3\times 60=180\text{ g/min}\). The alternative divides by the number of seconds in a minute instead of multiplying.
questions.hint: Decide how changing the time unit from seconds to minutes changes the rate.

questions.concept: Converting a Rate from per Hour to per Minute
questions.learningObjective: Convert a rate given per hour to the equivalent rate per minute.
questions.question: A conveyor moves \(7{,}200\text{ m/h}\). What is this rate in metres per minute?
questions.explanation:
There are \(60\text{ min}\) in one hour, so
\(7{,}200\div 60=120\text{ m/min}\). The alternative multiplies by the number of minutes in an hour instead of dividing.
questions.hint: Decide how changing the time unit changes a rate.

questions.concept: Converting a Rate from per Minute to per Hour with a Decimal Value
questions.learningObjective: Convert a decimal per-minute rate to the equivalent per-hour rate.
questions.question: A drone flies at \(0.5\text{ km/min}\). What is this rate in kilometres per hour?
questions.explanation:
There are \(60\text{ min}\) in one hour, so
\(0.5\times 60=30\text{ km/h}\). The alternative divides by the number of minutes in an hour instead of multiplying.
questions.hint: Write a unit conversion that cancels the unwanted time unit.

questions.concept: Converting a Rate from per Second to per Minute
questions.learningObjective: Convert a speed in \(\text{m/s}\) to the equivalent speed in \(\text{m/min}\).
questions.question: A robot moves at \(2\text{ m/s}\). What is this speed in metres per minute?
questions.explanation:
There are \(60\text{ s}\) in one minute, so
\(2\times 60=120\text{ m/min}\). The alternative divides by the number of seconds in a minute instead of multiplying.
questions.hint: Track the distance unit and the time unit separately.
